---
title: "Distance Calculation"
subtitle: Distance calculation to the nearest Norwegian coastline from site locations
---

As the initial data analysis will be performed on the Vannmiljø sites located within Norwegian fjords and surrounding areas near the Norwegian coastline, the distances to the nearest coastline were calculated.

The distance data is available in the `dist_to_coast` column of the [Site](db-schema.qmd#site-table) table.

## Methods

The distance is computed by [seastamp](https://github.com/AIQC-Hub/seastamp), the command line tool that annotates locations for every stage of the pipeline. Using one tool throughout means the pilot values agree with the ones the later generations carry, rather than differing in detail.

* **Shoreline data:** the **Global Self-consistent, Hierarchical, High-resolution Geography** ([GSHHG](https://www.soest.hawaii.edu/pwessel/gshhg/)) database at full resolution, the most detailed of its five levels.
* **Projection:** a **Lambert Azimuthal Equal Area** projection centred on the data. seastamp derives the extent from the sampling points themselves rather than applying a fixed global projection, which keeps distortion low at the high latitudes this survey reaches.
* **De-duplication:** coordinates are rounded to three decimal places before lookup, so sites repeated at one position are computed once.
* **Result:** the shortest distance from the site position to the nearest shoreline polygon, in kilometres.

::: {.callout-note}
### Recalculated at v0.1.24
These values were previously calculated in R with the [sf](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sf/index.html) library, against a GSHHG extract cropped to Norway and Svalbard and projected to EPSG:3035. Both approaches use GSHHG, so most distances barely moved: across the 21,300 distinct site positions the median change is 0.02 km.

The exception is worth knowing about. Six sites carry coordinates near the equator (4.511 E, 0.001 N), which are clearly wrong for a Norwegian monitoring programme. The old calculation measured them against the Norwegian coastline crop and returned 3,965 km; seastamp measures against the real nearest coast and returns 199 km, off West Africa. The distance is now correct, but the coordinates behind it are not: the later pipeline stages flag these sites rather than trusting them.
:::

## Sediment Core Locations with Distances to Coast

{{< include _db-setup.qmd >}}

```{ojs}
//| output: false

// --- Query site locations ---
df_loc = db.query(`
  SELECT DISTINCT
    a1.activity_id,
    s2.site_code,
    s2.lat  AS latitude,
    s2.lon  AS longitude,
    CASE
      WHEN s2.dist_to_coast <= 10  THEN '0 to 10km'
      WHEN s2.dist_to_coast <= 30  THEN '10 to 30km'
      WHEN s2.dist_to_coast <= 100 THEN '30 to 100km'
      ELSE '≥100km'
    END AS distance
  FROM sample s1
  JOIN activity a1 ON a1.activity_id = s1.activity_id
  JOIN site s2 ON s2.site_code = s1.site_code
`)

// --- World boundaries (Natural Earth via CDN) ---
world_topo = fetch("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/world-atlas@2/countries-50m.json")
  .then(r => r.json())

world_geojson = topojson.feature(world_topo, world_topo.objects.countries)

dist_counts = db.query(`
  SELECT distance AS Distance,
         COUNT(*) AS '# Sampling Sites'
  FROM (
      SELECT DISTINCT
        a1.activity_id,
        s2.site_code,
        s2.lat  AS latitude,
        s2.lon  AS longitude,
        CASE
          WHEN s2.dist_to_coast <= 10  THEN '0 to 10km'
          WHEN s2.dist_to_coast <= 30  THEN '10 to 30km'
          WHEN s2.dist_to_coast <= 100 THEN '30 to 100km'
          ELSE '≥100km'
        END AS distance
      FROM sample s1
      JOIN activity a1 ON a1.activity_id = s1.activity_id
      JOIN site s2 ON s2.site_code = s1.site_code
  ) t
  GROUP BY distance
`)

```

```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  width: 480,
  height: 560,
  marginRight: 120,
  caption: "Sediment Cores — LAEA Europe Projection",
  // Pass a D3 projection function directly — reliable regional zoom
  // Observable Plot calls it with the actual {width, height} at render time
  projection: ({width, height}) => {
    const mercY     = lat => Math.log(Math.tan(Math.PI / 4 + lat * Math.PI / 360))
    const yTop      = mercY(82), yBot = mercY(56)
    const yRange    = yTop - yBot
    const scale     = (height - 20) / yRange
    const yMid      = (yTop + yBot) / 2
    const latCenter = (Math.atan(Math.exp(yMid)) - Math.PI / 4) * 360 / Math.PI
    return d3.geoMercator()
      .center([13.5, latCenter])
      .scale(scale)
      .translate([width / 2, height / 2])
  },
  color: {
    domain: ["0 to 10km", "10 to 30km", "30 to 100km", "≥100km"],
    range:  ["#30123b",   "#28bbec",    "#a2fc3c",    "#fb8022"],
    legend: true,
    label:  "Distance to Coastline"
  },
  marks: [
    // Ocean background clipped to the domain frame
    Plot.frame({ fill: "#d0e8f5" }),
    // Country polygons — clip: "frame" trims anything outside the domain bbox
    Plot.geo(world_geojson, { fill: "#d4d4d4", stroke: "#888", strokeWidth: 0.4, clip: "frame" }),
    // Graticule grid lines clipped to frame
    Plot.graticule({ stroke: "gray", strokeWidth: 0.4, strokeDasharray: "3,3", clip: "frame" }),
    // Frame border drawn on top
    Plot.frame({ stroke: "#555", strokeWidth: 0.8 }),
    // Site locations coloured by distance category
    Plot.dot(df_loc, {
      x: "longitude",
      y: "latitude",
      fill: "distance",
      r: 3.5,
      fillOpacity: 0.85,
      stroke: "#222",
      strokeWidth: 0.3,
      clip: "frame"
    })
  ]
})
```

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(dist_counts, {
  columns: ["Distance", "# Sampling Sites"],
  layout: "fixed",
  width: { "Distance": "50%", "# Sampling Sites": "50%" }
})
```
